Definition: a strengthened form of a primary prio (to saw); to saw in two:--saw asunder.
BiblicalUsage: Prizo means to saw asunder, and the writer to the Hebrews uses it once, in the roll of the suffering faithful. They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, they were tempted, they were slain with the sword, and the world was not worthy of them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the sawn-asunder saints are the measure of faith, and their suffering is the price of a testimony the world could not bear.
